page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the Intel x86_64 processor architecture. The instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core running two execution threads, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. This maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Advanced CPU features including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets are present. The instance does not include local storage disks and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring reliance on external block storage and separately allocated networking resources.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-threaded responsiveness alongside strict multi-core throughput constraints resulting from the single physical core design. In single-core testing, the instance records average marks within its class, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 28.28 GB/sec. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded metrics place in the bottom percentiles, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 1714.68 and a PassMark CPU score of 2984.94. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 19.35 GB/sec, while Redis SET throughput reaches 2.43 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, n4-standard-2 delivers dedicated execution resources free from noisy-neighbor throttling common to burstable tiers, but total processing capacity is tightly capped. This profile is well defined for low-concurrency services rather than compute-bound compilation or dense parallel databases. Best-fit operational workloads include static web serving, lightweight microservices, development and testing environments, and low-scale background worker tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. The configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware vector extensions including AVX-512 and AMX are active, while local ephemeral storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. Benchmark testing highlights average single-thread throughput, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0 and gzip compression of 28.28 GB/sec. However, multi-core metrics sit in the lower quartile, reflecting the single-core physical topology under parallel load. Memory write bandwidth reaches 12.78 GB/sec and static web serving achieves 4.0 GB/sec. The n4-standard-2 is technically matched for modest enterprise workloads, such as low-traffic web serving, lightweight microservices, testing environments, and simple background task processing requiring dedicated CPU resources.
